bull.b: Initiating a global Phase III trial moves pemvidutide into a pivotal development stage in MASH and establishes a defined path toward regulatory evidence. Broad site coverage and planned enrollment provide an operational foundation for advancing the lead program over the next several quarters.

The breadth of RECLAIM results supports pemvidutide’s potential differentiation in AUD by combining reductions in drinking behavior, objective PEth improvement, and weight loss. Multiple clinically relevant endpoints strengthen the case for regulatory engagement and future development.

A substantial cash balance and stated funding through the PERFORMA 52-week readout give Altimmune greater ability to execute its central MASH program without an immediate financing requirement for that trial. This supports continuity of development and reduces near-term funding uncertainty.

bear.b: Altimmune has not yet established commercial revenue to offset research and development spending. Persistent large losses and substantial cash burn mean financial performance remains dependent on external capital or future clinical success, limiting operating self-sufficiency over the medium term.

The potential AUD pivotal trial would require additional financing beyond the stated runway. Management is considering royalties, debt, or partnerships, but those sources are not guaranteed, creating execution and funding uncertainty around expansion of the AUD opportunity.

Gastrointestinal tolerability monitoring could affect treatment persistence, while competition for MASH trial participants may pressure enrollment speed and costs. Together, these issues can complicate execution and extend the time or resources needed to generate pivotal evidence.
